title: Romance and dating
theme: A first date, a crush, a breakup, a partner others do not know about, an ex reappearing. Cozy, never explicit.

storylets.title: Two people, one bowl too many
storylets.note: A first meeting at the stalls. Awkward and sweet. Chain: rom.second-date or a fizzle.

A.desc: an adult dressed a little better than usual

b1: {A} stands by the pond, smoothing {A.his} jacket, and checks {A.his} reflection in a window.
{A} waits at the edge of the square, fixing a collar twice.
{A} stays by the koi pond and rolls both shoulders.
b2: {B.desc} arrives. {A} and {B.desc} greet each other with a stiff little nod and set off together.
{A} and {B.desc} cross toward the stalls, a careful arm's length apart.
{B.desc} falls in next to {A}. They walk without saying much.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} share a counter. {A} spills a little broth and wipes it up, laughing.
They split a bowl, trading small talk between sips.
{B.desc} offers {A} the last skewer. {A} offers it back.
b4: {A} and {B.desc} part at the pond with a wave each. Both are slow to turn away.
{B.desc} waves from the corner. {A} waves back and stays there a while.
{A} lifts a hand to {B.desc} across the square, then lowers it.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "So, {B.first}. How long have you lived on this side?"
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Call me {B.first}. Everybody does."
Overheard: {A} says: "We could do this again. Thursday, maybe, if you are free."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Thursday works. I know a better stall near the lift."

storylets.title: Thursday near the lift
storylets.note: Pays off rom.first-date. More easy than the first. Sets the pair as dating.

b1: {A} and {B.desc} meet at the foot of the lift and set off together, closer this time.
{B.desc} falls in beside {A}. Their steps match after a few paces.
{A} and {B.desc} cross the square. {B.desc} points out something on a roof.
b2: {A} and {B.desc} sit on a bench with a paper bag of buns between them.
{B.desc} takes a seat on the bench. {A} sits right next to {B.him}.
They settle on a bench, shoulders almost touching.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} talk until the lanterns come on.
{B.desc} laughs at something {A} says and shakes {B.his} head.
They talk low, the street going by in front of them.

storylets.title: The stall visited three times
storylets.note: Observation only: someone returns to the same counter over and over. No inner state is claimed.

B.desc: a stall worker behind the counter

b1: {A} joins the line at the stall and smooths {A.his} hair.
{A} gets in line, checks the menu board, and orders a small tea.
{A} waits in line at the counter, hands in pockets, eyes on the stall keeper.
b2: {A} lingers by the counter with the cup, facing the board.
{A} stays at the edge of the stall, a step from the register.
{A} loiters near the counter and looks at the pond.
b3: {B.desc} serves {A} a second cup without being asked and says a few words.
{B.desc} slides a cup over the counter. {A} nods too many times.
{B.desc} serves {A} and gets a very quick thanks.

log: {A} at this counter again: {seen} visits on the feed.
Back at the same counter. The feed has {A} here {seen} times.

storylets.title: A bunch of something green
storylets.note: Flowers handed over at a door or a lift base. Never explained.

A.desc: an adult with a small bouquet

b1: {A} comes up the walk with a handful of stems wrapped in paper.
{A} carries a small bunch of flowers up to {place}, holding it low.
{A} arrives at {place}, tugging the wrapping straight.
b2: The door slides open. {A} holds the bunch out. {B.desc} takes it and laughs.
{A} hands over the flowers with a small bow. {B.desc} presses a hand to {B.his} cheek.
{A} passes the stems across the threshold. {B.desc} looks at them, then at {A}.
b3: Both go in. The door slides shut on the paper.
{B.desc} pulls {A} inside by the sleeve.
{A} and {B.desc} go into {place} together.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "For my {B.rel}. Seven years today."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Seven years, and my {A.rel} still remembers."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "You remembered. Seven years and you still remember."
Overheard: {A} says: "Happy anniversary. The stall was out of the red ones."

storylets.title: A slow loop after dinner
storylets.note: A couple walks and sits. The pair stays unlabeled until someone says something.

b1: {A} and {B.desc} walk the square, fingers hooked together.
{A} and {B.desc} take the long way around the pond, in step.
{B.desc} links arms with {A} and steers toward the benches.
b2: {A} and {B.desc} sit on a bench and watch the lanterns flicker on.
{B.desc} takes a seat, and {A} settles in beside {B.him}, a jacket draped over both their laps.
They sit close, backs to the wall.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} talk in low voices. {B.desc} laughs at something.
{B.desc} leans against {A} and says a few words.
They talk about nothing in particular for a good while.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says to {A}: "Married five years and you still steal my side of the bench."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "My {A.rel} carries the bag. That's the deal."
Overheard: {A} says: "My love, it is your turn to carry the bag home."

storylets.title: The door that stayed open
storylets.note: A breakup mostly happens indoors. The street sees the end of it. Hearsay carries the rest.

A.desc: an adult leaving with a bag

B.desc: a partner standing in the doorway

b1: {A} comes out of {place} with a packed bag over one shoulder.
{A} leaves {place}, a jacket half on, a bag banging on {A.his} hip.
{A} steps out, a crate of belongings in both arms.
b2: {B.desc} calls from the doorway. {A} answers without turning. Voices rise and fall.
{A} and {B.desc} argue in the doorway, hands cutting the air.
{B.desc} holds the door and says a few words that make {A} stop.
b3: {A} walks off down the block and does not look back.
{A} crosses the street and keeps going.
{A} heads toward the metro with the bag held tight.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "I'll be at a friend's. Send the rest of my things there."
Overheard: {A} says: "Don't call. I'll call when I'm ready."

lines: Overheard: {S} tells {L} that {A.desc} and {A.his} partner split last week. A bag, an argument, and that was that.
Overheard: {S} says to {L}: "You heard? {A.desc} walked out of the apartment and has not been back."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} and {A.his} partner broke up and that the whole block heard the shouting.
Overheard: {S} mentions to {L} that {A.desc} is on {A.his} own now.
entry: Broke up with a partner last week (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Left a shared home after an argument, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Ended things with a partner, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: An old face by the pond
storylets.note: An ex crosses the square. Neither is quite sure what to do with their hands.

b1: {A} stands at the pond with a cup, looking at the water.
{A} stays by a planter, a cup in each hand.
{A} idles near the rail, scrolling slowly through {A.his} comm.
b2: {B.desc} rounds the stalls and nearly collides with {A}. Both freeze.
{A} turns and walks straight into {B.desc}, cup first. Both stop dead.
{B.desc} comes around a corner and halts a pace from {A}.
b3: They talk with stiff shoulders. {B.desc} laughs once, short.
{A} and {B.desc} trade a few careful sentences and look at their feet.
{B.desc} asks something and {A} answers in a word or two.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Strange, running into an {B.rel} by the pond."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Is it odd, an {A.rel} saying hello?"
Overheard: {A} says: "It has been two years. You cut your hair."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "I did. Good to see you. I should not keep you."

storylets.title: Hands in a coat pocket
storylets.note: A new relationship starts. The watcher sees a walk; hearsay supplies the rest.

A.desc: an adult walking with someone new

b1: {A} and {B.desc} stroll the block, their joined hands tucked into one coat pocket.
{A} and {B.desc} walk slowly, shoulders touching.
{B.desc} steers {A} around a puddle without letting go.
b2: They sit on a bench and share a drink with two straws.
{A} sits and {B.desc} sits close, the drink passing between them.
{A} and {B.desc} take the bench by the pond.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} hug, long and quiet.
{B.desc} pulls {A} in for a hug and does not let go for a while.
{A} hugs {B.desc} and then steps back, laughing.

lines: Overheard: {S} says to {L} that {A.desc} has been seeing someone new. The two were out on the benches most nights.
Overheard: {S} tells {L}: "{A.desc} is going out with someone new. Smiling all week, too."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} has found someone: "Saw them together with my own eyes."
Overheard: {S} mentions that {A.desc} has a new sweetheart and the whole block knows.
entry: Started seeing someone, as of last week (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Took up with someone new, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Was seen on the benches with a new companion, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: A folded note on the bench
storylets.note: A note found, picked up, put away. Nothing is read aloud.

b1: {A} sits on a bench and looks around the square.
{A} takes a seat on the bench and stretches both legs.
{A} perches on the edge of a bench with a cup.
b2: {A} retrieves a folded paper from the slats and smooths it flat.
{A} picks up a small folded note from the bench and turns it over.
{A} scoops a crumpled paper from beside {A.him} and unfolds it.
b3: {A} reads it, shrugs, and puts it in a pocket.
{A} turns away and folds the paper into a tight square.
{A} shakes {A.his} head and tucks it away.

log: Overheard: {A} says to no one: "Wrong bench, whoever you are."
Overheard: {A} mutters: "Somebody left a message for somebody else."

storylets.title: Dinner with a candle
storylets.note: A pair at the stalls with a gift. Anniversary or just a Thursday.

b1: {A} and {B.desc} stand at the counter, heads together over the menu.
{A} and {B.desc} order two bowls and a pair of sweet buns from the board.
{B.desc} orders for both. {A} adds two teas.
b2: {A} hands over a small flat box. {B.desc} opens it and stares.
{A} holds out a wrapped gift. {B.desc} turns it over twice.
{A} passes a small parcel across the counter.
b3: They eat slowly, chopsticks crossing in the same bowl.
{A} and {B.desc} tear a sweet bun in half and share it.
{B.desc} has the gift on before the bowl is empty.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Ten years, and still my favorite {A.rel}."
Overheard: {A} raises a cup: "To my {B.rel}. Ten years."
Overheard: {A} says: "Happy anniversary. Ten years. I counted the stalls we ate at."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "You and your counting. Come here."

storylets.title: A long goodnight at the door
storylets.note: A late call that outlasts the evening. One side only.

A.desc: an adult on a call outside a door

b1: {A} stands outside {place}, not going in.
{A} lingers by the door of {place}, a comm warm in one hand.
{A} paces a small circle outside {place}.
b2: {A} takes a call on {A.his} comm, back against the doorframe, voice soft.
{A} holds the comm to one ear and smiles at the ground.
{A} listens for a long time, then laughs under {A.his} breath.
b3: {A} goes into {place} at last, comm still in hand.
{A} enters and the door slides shut.
{A} steps in and the light behind the door comes on.

log: Comm, one side: {A} says: "Goodnight, love. I will see you at the lift at seven."
Comm, one side: {A} says: "You hang up first. No, you. Fine, together."

storylets.title: Posted with two hands in the frame
storylets.note: A feed post that puts a partner on the record. Public, vague and performative.

b1: {A} sits on a bench and holds a comm out at arm's length.
{A} takes a seat and frames a cup on the comm's screen.
{A} perches on the edge of the bench and angles the comm low.
b2: {A} posts a picture and puts the comm face down.
{A} types a line, adds a heart, and posts.
{A} posts and shows the screen to nobody.

log: Posted: "Two years today. Same cafe, same stool, still the best company."
Posted: "Dinner with my favorite person. Not sharing the skewers."
